edit.text:
This image is a template for 7 parallax backdrop layers of DAWNHARBOR, a white-walled port town at sunrise, in my game's style: soft painted pixel art, warm gold light, plum-violet shade. Replace each WHITE strip with the layer named on it, filling that strip edge to edge and staying inside it: nothing may cross a strip's top or bottom edge, so make each layer only as tall as its strip. The 6 MAGENTA rows between the strips are gaps: leave them untouched, flat magenta #FF00FF, with nothing painted on them, not even sky.
1. FAR LAYER: sky from navy #1d2f5c at the top through blue #3f6aa0 and peach #f2a98a to cream #ffe0b0, over the open sea with a distant line of hazy blue islands. Fills its strip; seamless left to right.
2. MID LAYER: rooftops of the port, white walls and blue tiles stepping up a hill, on magenta (no sky behind them). Seamless left to right.
3. NEAR LAYER: the harbour front, ship masts, rigging and furled sails, on magenta (no sky behind them). Seamless left to right.
4. CLOUDS: 4 separate soft morning clouds, cream with peach undersides, on magenta.
5. LANDMARK: a tall white lighthouse on a rocky point with a sun-shaped lamp, on magenta.
6. SKY BODY: a low warm morning sun with a soft glow ring, on magenta.
7. MOTES: a scatter of sparkles like sun on water and a few distant gulls, on magenta.
Remove the white and the label text: in strips 2 to 7 everything that is not part of the layer becomes flat magenta #FF00FF.

This is my sheet of 7 painted parallax backdrop layers for Lanternfall, a lantern-lit town at dusk. Keep the soft painted style, the colours, every strip's position and height, the labels and the divider lines exactly. Fix only these things:
1. FAR LAYER: the orange dusk sky behind the tower silhouettes must fill its whole strip as a solid rectangle, edge to edge: no fading into magenta at the left end, the right end or the top corners. Its left and right edges must match so the strip tiles sideways.
2. MID LAYER: keep as it is; make its left and right edges match so it tiles.
3. NEAR LAYER: fill the magenta gap in the middle of the alley with more timber houses, walls and doors like the rest of the strip, so the strip is solid edge to edge. Its left and right edges must match so it tiles.
4. CLOUDS: exactly 4 separate soft dusk clouds, one centred in each quarter of the strip, on flat magenta. Remove the castle, the village, the hill and the bridge from this strip.
5. LANDMARK: only the clock tower with its trees, on flat magenta. Remove the pink clouds behind it.
6. SKY BODY: only the round orange moon, on flat magenta, with no clouds and no pink glow around it.
7. MOTES: keep the lanterns and fireflies, on flat magenta, with no pink glow patches.
Everything that is not part of a layer is flat pure magenta #FF00FF.

On it, paint ONE new building for Emberforge, the warriors' forge town in my 2D side-scrolling game: proud, hot, hardworking and heroic, built among cinder hills and volcanic ridges, lit by warm amber forge light under an ember-brown sky. The second image shows four of my game's NPC characters; they are drawn in exactly the art style the whole game must have: soft cel-painted shading with clear light and shadow shapes and bright highlights on the lit edges, rich warm saturated colours, bold dark brown outlines, and plenty of hand-painted detail (stone blocks, wood grain, iron rivets, soot, worn and chipped spots, slight colour variation between stones and roof tiles). Use this palette: grey stone blocks, terracotta roof tiles, dark oak beams, black iron straps and rivets, and orange forge-lit windows. The new building is the WARRIORS' HALL, the grandest building in the town, a little wider than it is tall: a solid two-storey hall of big grey stone blocks on a heavy dark stone plinth, with stout square stone buttresses at both corners; a steep terracotta tile roof with a raised central gable; two tall stone chimneys with iron caps, one at each end of the roof; a big arched oak double door in the middle of the ground floor, bound with black iron straps and studded with rivets; tall narrow windows on both floors glowing warm orange from the forge-light inside, with iron bars; a large round shield with crossed swords mounted on the gable above the door; two long crimson cloth banners with a gold crossed-swords emblem (pictures only, no writing) hanging flat against the wall on either side of the door, fixed at top and bottom; a pair of iron braziers fixed flat to the wall beside the door, each with a small steady flame. Strict rules: 1) Pure front view at eye level: only the front face shows, no roof surface seen from above, every horizontal line level and every wall edge vertical. 2) The bottom of the whole building is ONE straight horizontal line: its stone plinth reaches down to the same ground line from edge to edge, with nothing hanging lower. Nothing below the base or in front of it: no steps, path, ground patch, ground line, rubble, people or shadow. 3) The door is a real doorway at ground level, centred left to right in the building. 4) The whole building fits inside the picture, centred, with a clear band of magenta on every side. 5) Painted, not pixel art: smooth painted shading with visible soft brush texture, no visible pixels. No letters or words anywhere. No blue roof tiles or cream plaster (that is a different town). Nothing (rope, cloth, chain) ends loose in mid-air. No smoke or glow spilling onto the background. Flat pure magenta #FF00FF background everywhere outside the building, with no magenta or pink anywhere inside it. Do not draw any characters.

edit.text: The first image is a blank canvas showing only a soft colour gradient. Repaint the whole canvas as ONE complete, seamless, highly detailed background painting for Emberforge, the warriors' forge town in my 2D side-scrolling game: proud, hot, hardworking and heroic, built among cinder hills and volcanic ridges, lit by warm amber forge light under an ember-brown sky. The second image shows four of my game's NPC characters; they are drawn in exactly the art style the whole game must have: soft cel-painted shading with clear light and shadow shapes and bright highlights on the lit edges, rich warm saturated colours, bold dark brown outlines, and plenty of hand-painted detail (stone blocks, wood grain, iron rivets, soot, worn and chipped spots, slight colour variation between stones and roof tiles). Paint the background in that same style, a little softer and lighter in contrast so it sits behind the characters. Use a palette of grey stone, terracotta roofs and warm orange forge-light. The scene: a range of dark volcanic ridges and jagged cinder peaks seen across a wide valley at dusk. The ridges stand in layers, the nearest in the middle distance in deep brown-grey rock, the farther ones fading back into warm orange-red haze. One big dormant volcano in the far distance has a faint orange glow at its crater and a soft column of grey smoke drifting up. Thin glowing lava streams trickle down a few far slopes. In the middle distance, the silhouettes of a few stone forge buildings with terracotta roofs and tall chimneys sit on terraces cut into a ridge, their windows glowing orange, the chimneys letting out soft grey smoke; a stone viaduct with arches crosses between two ridges. Small glowing embers drift upward through the whole scene. Colours: dark ember-brown at the very top of the sky (#24120c), warming to a bright orange horizon (#ffb060) with amber light (#ffd0a0), and an orange-red haze (#bf592f) low in the valley. Warm and heroic, not dark or scary. Strict rules: 1) Side-on view at eye level, as if standing in the town looking out, the horizon level. 2) No people, no characters, no animals, no birds, no dragons. 3) Nothing in the near foreground: no ground, rocks, rubble or plants in front; the closest things are in the middle distance. 4) The left and right edges continue naturally (ridges and haze), nothing is cut in half at the edges. 5) Fill the whole canvas edge to edge with painting; no border, no frame, no magenta. 6) Painted, not pixel art: smooth painted shading with visible soft brush texture, no visible pixels. Cell 1 holds one flat bright green (#00FF00) shape: the exact outline of the boy in the same cell of the first attached picture, in the same pose (cell 1: seen from BEHIND, his back to the viewer, mid backhand slash: one arm stretched out to the right at shoulder height, the other arm folded across his chest). Cells 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are empty and must stay empty. The second attached picture shows this exact piece already painted on the same boy: copy its colours, materials, shape and details exactly, never its poses. On each green shape, paint ONLY loose magician's trousers worn on his legs from the waist to the ankles: soft light-tan cloth, loose and a little baggy, gathered at the ankles, with visible seams. They follow his legs in each pose, however they bend, stretch, kneel or tuck, and cover each leg whole down to where the foot begins. Each piece is exactly the size of the green body part it covers: never blown up, never filling the cell, never a separate standing figure. He is seen from BEHIND, so paint the BACK of the piece as it would look from behind: no buttons, buckles, lacing or front details that only show from the front. Keep every green shape exactly where it is, in its own pose; do not redraw any pose. Paint nothing else: no head, hands, other clothing, gear, weapons or objects. The green shape is only a flat placement guide lying BEHIND everything you paint, never in front of it: paint each piece WHOLE straight over the green, including right across the green arms, hands and fists where they cross it, with no gaps, notches, bites or holes anywhere; parts an arm will hide later are still painted completely. Check every cell for holes before finishing. Leave every part of each green shape you do not paint over flat pure #00FF00 green, exactly as it is, and leave the rest of the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. Do not move, resize or redraw any shape, and do not add any figure. Leave empty cells empty. Style: warm colours, light from the upper left, smooth soft painted shading with bright highlights, thin dark plum-brown outline, small busy painted detail, like the painted villagers in the third attached picture. edit.text: The first image is a guide on a flat magenta #FF00FF background showing four objects for my 2D side-scrolling game as flat colour shapes. Paint each one over its shape as a finished object for a small, ordinary seaside town that was abandoned and fell to ruin long ago, keeping each shape's position, size and outline EXACTLY. The whole place is drained of colour: ash greys, pale blue-greys and faded driftwood browns under a flat, sunless, overcast light; quiet and sad, never scary, no blood, no bones, no fire, no plants growing, nobody there. 1) LEFT, a ruined cottage front: a plain whitewashed stone cottage wall, its roof gone, the top of the wall broken into jagged crumbling stone, the plaster cracked and flaking to show grey stones beneath; the two dark squares are empty window holes with a broken shutter hanging from one; the dark doorway is an empty opening with no door. 2) MIDDLE, a broken wooden lookout: an old weathered wooden watchtower of two tall posts with a cross brace and a plank deck on top; the top rail has snapped and hangs at an angle, one rail post is broken short; the wood is grey, split and salt-worn, with rusty iron bolts. 3) RIGHT TOP, a lone standing wall: all that is left of a house, a section of grey stone wall with a crumbling top and an empty door frame, its doorway open onto nothing. 4) RIGHT BOTTOM, an upturned old rowboat lying on the sand, its grey planks cracked, with a broken hole in its side (the dark shape). Style: clean, simple and strongly readable shapes with little clutter, like the hand-made world of Hollow Knight, but in my game's own painted style: soft cel-painted shading with clear light and shadow shapes, soft pale highlights on the lit edges from the upper left, a bold dark outline, and hand-painted texture at a fairly chunky brush scale (stone, cracked plaster, wood grain, worn and chipped spots). edit.text: The base picture is an EMPTY sheet of 8 cells (2 rows of 4, numbered left to right, then top to bottom) on a flat magenta background. Paint ONE frame of a single skill effect animation in each cell, so that cells 1 to 8 played in order make one smooth, exciting animation. This is a flashy movement skill in a hand-painted 2D fantasy side-scroller, grand and spectacular like the skill effects of MapleStory, but painted: luminous hand-painted light with visible, fairly chunky brush strokes and painted texture, rich saturated colour, a white-hot core fading through bright colour to soft glowing edges, strong contrast between the bright core and the deeper colour around it. Never pixel art, never a photo, never a 3D render, never flat vector shapes. The skill is SLAM, a straight drop from the air that smashes down onto the floor, in molten light: white-hot yellow, blazing orange and deep ember red. This sheet is its IMPACT where he lands: the effect sits on an invisible floor line across the lower third of each cell, centred, spreading sideways along it, about three quarters of the cell's width at its biggest. Cell 1: a short bright downward streak of light hitting the floor line. Cell 2: a white-hot flash bursting at the point of impact. Cell 3: a low dome of blazing orange light pushing up and out, with sharp molten rays. Cell 4: the peak, a wide flat shockwave racing out left and right along the floor line, a fountain of glowing ember sparks flying up and out. Cell 5: the shockwave widening and thinning, sparks arcing down. Cell 6: two thin fading glowing arcs at the far left and right, embers falling. Cell 7: scattered dim embers. Cell 8: a few last tiny embers. Every frame is the SAME effect at the same scale and in the same colours, anchored at the same place in its cell; only its animation stage changes, so the frames flow smoothly from one to the next. It is light and magic, so it has NO outline at all: no dark line or border around any arc, flame, spark or glow; its edges are light fading softly into the background. Draw ONLY the effect: no character, hero, foot, hand, weapon, monster, creature, face, ground, floor, rocks, rubble, grass, scenery, shadow on the ground, text, title, letters or numbers anywhere. No smoke clouds. Each frame fits fully inside its own cell with a wide clear magenta margin on every side, never touching or crossing a cell border; never merge, split or add cells. Keep only the base picture's grid lines: never add extra grid lines, guide lines, boxes, squares or subdivisions inside any cell, and never fill a cell with grey or any colour. REPAINT: the background stays exactly the base picture's bright pure flat magenta #FF00FF (RGB 255, 0, 255) in every cell, never a darker plum or wine colour, never white, grey, black, pink or mauve, with no gradient or glow haze spreading into it beyond the effect's own soft edge. The effect itself uses NO pink, magenta, purple or violet anywhere.
